headline: Microsoft's November Windows 11 patch fixes flaws but hits install errors
summary: Microsoft released its November Patch Tuesday cumulative updates for Windows 11 (KB5132061 and KB5131087), fixing over a thousand security flaws, adding a customizable File Explorer right-click menu, and resolving a USB audio issue dating to September. Some users reported the update failing to install, throwing specific error codes, with no comment from Microsoft.

claims.statement: Microsoft released its November Patch Tuesday cumulative updates for Windows 11 (KB5132061 and KB5131087) to fix security vulnerabilities and bugs and add features.

sources.quote: Windows 11 KB5132061 & KB5131087 cumulative updates released
Microsoft has released the Patch Tuesday Windows 11 and cumulative updates for versions 26H2/25H2/24H2 and 23H2 to fix security vulnerabilities and bugs, and add new features.

claims.statement: The update let users customize the File Explorer right-click menu and fixed 1,094 security flaws, including an actively exploited one.

sources.quote: New Windows 11 update fixes File Explorer menu mess – and patches an exploited flaw
With the November Patch Tuesday rollout, you can finally customize your right-click menu in Windows 11. It fixes 1,094 security flaws, too.

claims.statement: The same update resolved a USB audio issue that had been affecting Windows users since the September security updates.

sources.quote: Microsoft fixes audio issues caused by September security updates
Microsoft says the November 2026 cumulative updates resolve USB audio issues plaguing Windows users who have installed security updates released since September.

claims.statement: Some users experienced KB5132061 failing to install, throwing specific error codes, with no comment from Microsoft.

sources.quote: Microsoft's Patch Tuesday can't break stuff if it won't install
KB5132061 throws 0x800F0993 and 0x800F0989 errors, and Redmond is saying nothing
